newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican bourse head says stock growth could slow.
newsitem.headline: Mexican bourse head says stock growth could slow.

text.p: The outlook for Mexican stocks is still very favorable, but the pace of growth seen in the bourse is likely to slow, Mexican stock market president Manuel Robleda said on Wednesday.

"We've seen very significant gains, but we have to understand that it is not possible for it can continue, or it is not so likely that the market keep growing in terms of gains at the same rhythm," Robleda said in an interview with Radio Red.
Mexican stocks have seen gains of about 43 percent in dollar and peso terms since beginning of the year, he added.

Mexico's blue-chip IPC index reached a new record on Tuesday, closing up 79.90 points at 4,8321.14. Dealers and analysts have attributed the flurry of recent stock highs to investor relief at relatively clean elections and an improved economic outlook.
"The economic program is working," Robleda said. "We are expecting to see improved earnings in the second quarter."
Mexican corporate earnings are expected at the month's end. Robleda said they should be more favorable than last quarter, when he said about one in every five companies reported losses.
He also cited indicators from the futures market, lower sovereign debt and inflation, in estimating that the bourse will continue to improve in the near term.
